final.scope: Actual compiled main archive viewer; synchronous attributed capture through visible controls

changes: Apposed dextral whorl volumes and a limited aperture recess replace the earlier smooth conical envelope. A reflected white columellar lip is distinguished from the brown outer rim.
A closed connected external head-foot-mantle replaces separate head/neck/foot primitives. The selected sole supports the display body; shell carriage and collar insertion remain unfitted.
Two closed flattened cephalic tentacles have attached transverse bands and small basal eyes. They retain the periwinkle form rather than Lymnaea triangular feelers or four land-snail stalks.

A selected posterior corneous opercular exterior is included, with its incomplete attachment and closure explicitly disclosed. Original numerical pigment remains artwork, not a photographic skin scan.
The existing local tentacle study is finite, returns to neutral and holds. The archive does not call it crawling, feeding or physiological retraction.
A separately licensed extended-body photograph adds a useful comparison with the retained withdrawn-animal profile image. Exact derivative and delivery hashes are recorded.
limitations: This remains a partly stylized, unmeasured adult exterior. Whorl shape/apposition, the selected 5.5 turns and 0.8-radian oblique axis, aperture and mantle insertion, shell thickness, snout, foot outline, basal eyes and posterior opercular attachment are authored choices, not a specimen fit. The apertural recess is limited; a complete internal columella, pallial organs, opercular seal and physiological retraction are absent. The selected pigment and bands omit much natural wear, epibionts and individual variation, and do not calibrate tissue scattering or wet-shell optics. Basal eyes and the partly concealed operculum need further anatomical work. The same body performs only one finite local tentacle gesture; crawling, pedal waves, stationary interwaves, mucus/traction, grazing, respiration, contact forces and physiology remain unfinished. The extended photograph has an oblique seaweed pose and partly occluded feelers; it does not validate the selected level support or a gait. Compatibility/export omits fine main-shader bands. No measured accuracy percentage, independent specialist validation or completed photorealism is claimed.
testHistory: The first candidate used exposed swept surfaces that separated visibly into a corkscrew and left an empty upper aperture. Those views were rejected. A closed implicit union now apposes selected whorl volumes with a limited aperture recess. Later candidates had high upright carriage, oversized close-up cameras and an overhanging anterior head; oblique carriage, a refitted collar, broader anterior sole and region-specific framing were revised after actual views. Initial generator/revision checks retained the wrong old species epithet; that mapping was corrected. A later sentence-format expectation and the old open-sheet 80-edge topology expectation were repaired without discarding support/reset/hash checks: the new closed shell must be connected, and a direct ray check must confirm the recessed aperture rather than a solid end cap. Private drafts are excluded from final screenshot counts.

None of these private drafts are final admission captures or a fitted specimen/biomechanical result.
